text: On February 11, 2019, the People Equity and Human Rights Division (PEHR) and the City Clerk's Office held an information session to provide information to the persons with disabilities community on the requirements and recruiting processes for appointments to public boards, committees, and tribunals. Participant feedback during the information session indicated that there are citizen concerns regarding the diversity of appointments to City boards, committees and tribunals, with particular regard to the lack of representation of persons with disabilities. Participants also discussed the potential unconscious bias on the part of the selection committee, as well as qualification requirements that exclude capable applicants. The Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee recommends that: 1. The Executive Committee direct the City Clerk, in consultation with the Executive Director, People, Equity and Human Rights and key community stakeholders, to report back to the Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee, on September 26, 2019, with a strategy to strengthen the recruitment and civic appointment selection process for public appointments to City boards, committees and tribunals, with the goal of increasing representation of persons with disabilities, and striving toward equitable representation by the year 2025.
